Main charitable entity types: Association (forening): no Greenlandic or Danish registration act for ordinary associations - it exists from its founding general meeting (freedom of association) and registers in the Danish-run CVR register under Inatsisartutlov nr. 33 of 28 Nov 2016 on registration in the Central Business Register (GER abolished 1 Jan 2018); foundation (fond): Danish Act on Foundations and Certain Associations applied by royal decree - Anordning nr. 917 of 15 Dec 1998 on entry into force for Greenland, as amended by Anordning nr. 2460 of 14 Dec 2021 (consolidated as LTA 2021 nr. 2702); fondsmyndighed = Danish Minister of Justice (Civilstyrelsen), with statutes also filed with Skattestyrelsen (Akileraartarnermut Aqutsisoqarfik), Nuuk
Key local requirements: Statutes must name a Greenlandic municipality as seat (hjemsted) and the CVR office requires a Greenlandic postal address; association: founding general meeting + board, no nationality rule or member minimum in statute; foundation (assets DKK 1m+): min. assets DKK 1,000,000 at founding (lower only with fondsmyndighed permission), board of at least 3, director(s) and at least half the board resident 'her i landet' unless the fondsmyndighed exempts, founder and family may not form a board majority without consent, statutes + board list to fondsmyndighed and municipal tax authority within 3 months; online CVR filing on virk.dk needs MitID (CPR) - others use paper forms sent to cvr@nanoq.gl; filings in Danish or Greenlandic (official language per Inatsisartutlov nr. 7 of 19 May 2010 on language policy), English guidance only
Est. cost & time: No government fee for CVR registration; local lawyer/accountant in Nuuk to draft Danish-language statutes and file roughly DKK 10,000-30,000 (~US$1,500-4,500, market estimate, unpublished); association 2-6 weeks to CVR number, plus 1-3 months for a tax-exemption decision; foundation also needs DKK 1m (~US$150,000) endowment and Civilstyrelsen dealings, 2-4 months
Notes: Greenland's own tax system (Skattestyrelsen, aka.gl) governs tax exemption; private-law fonde rules remain Danish law applied by royal decree (Anordning 917/1998, in force 1 Jan 1999; 2021 amendment added beneficial-owner registration in Erhvervsstyrelsen's IT system) | Foundations with assets under DKK 1m fall outside most of the act but still need statutes and beneficial-owner registration (s.1(6)) | Ordinary associations are not supervised; chapter 12 of the anordning only covers trade/employer associations | Associations may operate unregistered, but aka.gl warns that without a CVR number opening a bank account and receiving public funds is difficult | Greenland's CVR register merged into the Danish CVR on 1 Jan 2018 (Inatsisartutlov nr. 33/2016); Greenlandic guidance at aka.gl/sullissivik.gl | Feb 2025 Inatsisartut urgent law bans foreign donations to political parties - does not target charities
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Practical need for Greenland-resident board members - foundations must have at least half the board resident unless exempted, and banks verify each association board member with a Greenlandic residence certificate.
Registration fee (USD): none (CVR registration of associations/foundations has no published government fee; Civilstyrelsen may levy administration charges on foundations under anordning s.36, amount unpublished)
Time to register: 2-6 weeks (association CVR number); 2-4 months for a foundation incl. fondsmyndighed filings and tax-exemption ruling
Charitable deduction regime: No general donor deduction: the consolidated Greenland income tax act (Landstingslov nr. 12 of 2 Nov 2006, Selvstyrets lovbekendtgørelse nr. 62 of 24 Sep 2025) contains no gift deduction for charities - the Danish Ligningsloven s.8 A deduction and Danish approved-charity list do not apply to Greenlandic taxpayers; businesses can deduct only genuine operating expenses (s.24, e.g. sponsorship as marketing).
Foreign donor / donation restrictions: None notable for charities; foundations must report significant donors/contributors to the fondsmyndighed within 4 weeks of receipt (anordning s.1(3)); the 2025 ban on foreign donations applies only to political parties and politicians.
Annual compliance & reporting: Associations and foundations file financial statements with Skattestyrelsen every year even when tax-exempt (aka.gl); foundations: accounts per good accounting practice signed within 6 months of year-end, mandatory audit (state-authorised/registered auditor if equity DKK 3m+, auditor resident unless exempted), auditor appointment notified within 3 months, beneficial owners (board) registered and reviewed annually; board changes reported with the tax return; fines for missed filings (anordning s.40, s.50).
Tax-exempt status & benefits: Non-commercial associations are taxable only on business income (income tax act s.1(1) nr.14, s.1(3)) and can apply by email to Skattestyrelsen for exemption if non-profit, non-distributing and democratic; foundations are fully taxable (s.1(1) nr.13) but may be wholly/partly exempted where statutory purpose is charitable/public-benefit (s.3(2), decision by Naalakkersuisut); self-owning educational/social/cultural institutions exempt (s.3(1) nr.6). No donor-deduction benefit attaches.
Bank account (remote feasibility): Effectively blocked: only two banks - GrønlandsBANKEN (BANK of Greenland) and the former BankNordik Greenland branch (Bankivik since 2025) - and GrønlandsBANKEN's association onboarding requires CVR documentation, board-signed statutes and founding-meeting minutes, and two IDs per board member including a Greenlandic residence certificate (bopælsattest) under 1 year old; non-resident boards need case-by-case approval under Danish/Greenlandic AML rules, so a Danish bank or EMI is the realistic fallback.
